checks: Checked 0c3c4405d9ae2dd3 §1, (1)–(2), against its source digest, including the explicit interval case. Z is closed by continuity of the support functions.

For a regular x on L with normal u in a Borel subset of Z, u·x=h_L(u)=h_K(u) puts x in the exposed face of K. If x is regular for K, that supporting direction is its only normal. The exceptional points of K have zero ambient H^(d−1), hence also zero measure on the intersection with ∂L. This proves domination for arbitrary Borel subsets of Z, including atomic or singular normal mass.

The compact outer-normal relation gives the Borel regular locus by projecting the compact pairs of normals separated by at least 1/m. On the regular locus uniqueness and compactness give relative continuity. Local Lipschitz graph charts give the almost-everywhere regularity used in the comparison.

For the midpoint corollary in d≥2, the two full-dimensional endpoints have greatest common submeasure by the pointwise minimum of their normal densities. Both have weight 1/2 in M. Restrict its domination by S_M to Z and use the first part for M⊆K. In d=1 each interval has unit mass at both normal signs, so both assertions follow directly.

dependencies.application: For d≥2 take r=2, λ_1=λ_2=1/2, a_1=a_2=1, and ν=S_A∧S_B, which each full-dimensional body dominates. This gives ν≤S_M before restriction to Z. The d=1 assertion is independent of this predecessor.
